title: the-sorted-door-speaks-the-receiver-rule
intention: The /sorted door's proof fixture carries a WATCHME spec complete under the receiver rule, and the door's no-workflow field floor names a missing receiver in the same pass, so the door and cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py never disagree about a complete spec.
why: Measured 2026-10-01: fa4a411c96be's receiver rule turned skills/sorted/proofs/test_sorted_door.py red (rc 0 before the build, rc 1 after) because its fixture spec carries no receiver; lived symptom: the /sorted door's own proof stops vouching for the door, and its no-workflow floor under-reports a missing receiver.
traces_to: Law 1: one opinion about a complete WATCHME spec — the door's judgment IS watchme_spec_error, and its fallback floor reads that module's constants. RULE 1: the door's change and proof live in skills/sorted.
how: In skills/sorted/proofs/test_sorted_door.py the GOOD packet's watchme dict (line 85) gains "receiver": {"what": "the sorted door reads the door-health verdict", "in": "skills/sorted"}. In skills/sorted/door.py import RECEIVER_FIELD beside REQUIRED_FIELDS and BERTH_FIELD from cairn.tools.base.watchme_spec, and in the no-workflow branch (line ~152) add: if not isinstance(spec.get(RECEIVER_FIELD), dict): missing.append(RECEIVER_FIELD), so the floor's message names it. A new tooth in test_sorted_door.py: a packet with an unparseable workflow and a watchme lacking a receiver is refused with 'receiver' in the watchme lack's why. Lands after fa4a411c96be's build (it adds RECEIVER_FIELD).
falsifier: RED if: (1) skills/sorted/proofs/test_sorted_door.py exits non-zero with fa4a411c96be built; (2) a packet whose workflow does not parse and whose watchme lacks a receiver is refused without 'receiver' in the watchme lack's why, or passes. Horizon: the tester seal.
watchme: none, because the /sorted door at skills/sorted/door.py is itself the receiver: every cast passes through it, and a disagreement with watchme_spec_error shows as a refused or wrongly-passed cast at the very next /sorted
children: none, because the change is one fixture field, one floor check and one tooth in skills/sorted
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Which watchme? the GOOD dict's, line 85 of test_sorted_door.py; live_good (line 302) inherits it via dict(GOOD, ...). (2) Where is the floor? door.py lines 148-158, the else of 'if wf is not None'. (3) How does the proof register teeth? it is one main() with ok(name, cond, detail) lines and a PROVES dict at line 33; add the new ok line inside main and its name to PROVES under this ticket's id as clause 2, and the file's own exit as clause 1 via the composite convention the existing PROVES uses.

decisions.text: THE STEPS, IN ORDER, with the code (measured 2026-10-01). Step 1 (red tooth, skills/sorted/proofs/test_sorted_door.py): (a) extend PROVES with a second key: "7d2a4bbec455": {"1": "conforming cast berths", "2": "unparseable workflow names the missing receiver"}. (b) Insert, just above the comment '# 15-17. a conforming cast rides the seam' (line ~271), this block: no_wf = dict(GOOD, workflow='not a workflow at all'); then try: door.fire(no_wf, **roots); ok('unparseable workflow names the missing receiver', False, 'door passed a packet with no parseable workflow') / except DoorRefused as exc: ok('unparseable workflow names the missing receiver', 'receiver' in whys_of(exc, 'watchme'), whys_of(exc, 'watchme')). GOOD's watchme today has no receiver, so that new ok reds (the floor names only object/five fields/probe) AND the existing door.fire(dict(GOOD), **roots) at line ~272 raises DoorRefused (fa4a's gate rule faults the receiver-less spec) — the file exits non-zero: both clauses red before the build. Commit that red. Step 2 (build, two edits): (a) in GOOD's watchme dict (line ~85) add the key "receiver": {"what": "the sorted door reads the door-health verdict", "in": "skills/sorted"} — skills/sorted/intention+why.json exists in the REAL repo, which is what watchme_spec checks (_REPO_ROOT / in / intention+why.json), so the tmp fixture repo does not matter; the bad/triple-defect packets that replace watchme wholesale are untouched. (b) in skills/sorted/door.py add RECEIVER_FIELD to the 'from cairn.tools.base.watchme_spec import (BERTH_FIELD, REQUIRED_FIELDS, watchme_spec_error)' list (alphabetical: after BERTH_FIELD), and in the else-branch of 'if wf is not None:' (the no-workflow floor, line ~152), after the missing = [...] comprehension, add: if not isinstance(spec.get(RECEIVER_FIELD), dict): missing.append(RECEIVER_FIELD) — and change the 'if missing:' message tail from 'the gate reads five fields plus the probe berth' to 'the gate reads five fields, the probe berth and the receiver'. Step 3: run the proof green twice, commit, seal with python3 -m cairn.devices.tester.cli --seal skills/sorted/proofs/test_sorted_door.py. No other file moves.

whys_of is ALREADY DEFINED at skills/sorted/proofs/test_sorted_door.py line 54, verbatim: def whys_of(exc: DoorRefused, field: str) -> str: return ' | '.join(l['why'] for l in exc.lacks if l['field'] == field). It returns ONE STRING (every lack's why for that field joined by ' | '), so 'receiver' in whys_of(exc, 'watchme') is a substring test on that text, and the string is passed as ok()'s detail as-is. Nothing is added or imported for it.

Measured in skills/sorted/door.py at HEAD: the no-workflow floor's message is the string concatenation "spec is missing " + ", ".join(missing) + " — the gate reads five fields plus the probe berth; a partial spec is a watch nobody can arm" (three string literals, lines ~156-158). The build replaces 'five fields plus the probe berth' with 'five fields, the probe berth and the receiver' and appends RECEIVER_FIELD to missing when spec.get(RECEIVER_FIELD) is not a dict.
